title: People Rally Across the US to Get Voters to Vote Early
summary:
On Saturday, people held rallies in cities and towns across the United States. They wanted voters to vote early in the midterm elections. Midterm elections happen in the middle of a president's four-year term. Election Day this year is November 3.

A group called No Kings planned the rallies. The group is against President Donald Trump. Organizers said the events were nonpartisan, which means not tied to one political party.

In Washington, D.C., a band played near the Lincoln Memorial. Even in chilly weather, people danced. Signs said "VOTE EARLY."

In Atlanta, City Councilman Michael Julian Bond said voting is like a superpower. "Be a super hero, use your power," he said.

Voting by mail is a topic people disagree about. Trump has claimed, without evidence, that voting fraud cost him the 2020 election. On Thursday, his government sued election officials in California over how some mail-in ballots are counted.
why_it_matters: Voting is how people choose their leaders, and one day you will get to vote too.
